official.deadline_note: The 2025-26 call opened on 31 December 2025 and closed on 31 March 2026; no date for the next annual call is published yet.
official.status_note: The Indian National Science Academy call page for 2025-26 states 'Last date of proposal submission is 31 March 2026', which has passed; INSA publishes no open round at the verification date.
benefits: Fellowship allowance of Rs. 50,000 per month which includes accommodation and medical facilities as available to host institutes
Rs. 10,000 as a one-time contingency grant to the fellow scientist
Rs. 20,000 as a one-time contingency research grant for the host scientist through the institution

Round-trip economy air fare from the place of employment in the home country to the Indian host institute via the shortest route, plus local road or rail transport between the nearest airport and the host institute
Up to 80 fellowships (10 per country) awarded annually
eligibility: Citizen or permanent resident of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka or Thailand
Actively engaged in research at a university or research institution in their country in science and technology including engineering and medical sciences
Minimum qualification of PhD, M.Tech, M.Sc or MBBS with 3-5 years of research or teaching experience; applicants registered for a PhD degree in the home country may also apply
Below 45 years of age as on 31 March 2026
Valid passport and no visa for temporary or permanent residency in India
The fellowship may be availed only once during a period of five years
requirements: Apply on the prescribed ISRF format downloadable from www.dst.gov.in or www.insaindia.res.in
Applications must be duly endorsed by the Head of the home institution

Submit to the implementing agency in the partner country where one exists, with a copy to DST/INSA; otherwise send the hard copy or scan copy with supporting documents to the Executive Director, INSA, New Delhi, and the soft copy to isrf.dst@insa.nic.in
Finalise the fellowship dates jointly with the Indian host scientist after the selection
documents: Prescribed ISRF application form with a brief write-up describing the proposed research work
Copy of the degree certificate for the highest qualification
Reprints of two recent publications in refereed journals
Letter of Acceptance from the Indian host supervisor on institute letterhead and No Objection Certificate from the home institution
Two passport-size photographs and latest CV
selection_criteria: Pre-screening of applications by the implementing agency in the partner country, solely on scientific merit and the proposed contribution to advanced research
Final selection and fellowship decision by the Department of Science and Technology through its implementing agency INSA, New Delhi
Applications considered once a year by a Selection Committee; up to 80 fellowships are awarded annually, 10 per country
coverage: Fellowship allowance of Rs. 50,000 per month including accommodation and medical facilities as available to host institutes
Rs. 10,000 one-time contingency grant to the fellow and Rs. 20,000 one-time contingency research grant to the host scientist through the institution
Round-trip economy air fare and local transport between the nearest airport and the host institute
application_method: Download the prescribed ISRF application form from the INSA or DST website
Have the application endorsed by the Head of the home institution and obtain the Letter of Acceptance from the Indian host supervisor and the No Objection Certificate from the home institution
Submit to the implementing agency in the partner country (copying DST/INSA) or, where none exists, to INSA New Delhi as hard or soft copy with the scan copy to isrf.dst@insa.nic.in
After selection, finalise dates with the host scientist; the visa is issued by the Indian Mission in the candidate's country on the basis of the award
official.application_route: Prescribed form routed through the partner country's implementing agency or directly to INSA, New Delhi
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens or permanent residents of the eight listed countries; applicants must not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India
official.international_eligibility: Yes - restricted to citizens or permanent residents of the eight listed countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research in frontier or advanced areas of science including medicine and agriculture; applicants must be actively engaged in research in science and technology including engineering and medical sciences
official.research_requirement: A research proposal for a 3-6 month visiting fellowship at an Indian host institute; the fellow must submit a detailed research report after the tenure, endorsed by the host researcher
official.description: The India Science and Research Fellowship, funded by the Department of Science and Technology and administered by INSA, enables researchers from eight South and Southeast Asian countries to undertake R&D at premier Indian research and academic institutions for 3-6 months, paying a monthly allowance of Rs. 50,000 that includes accommodation and medical facilities where available, contingency grants, round-trip economy air fare and reimbursement of the visa fee.
official.program_type: Visiting research fellowship (not a degree programme)

not_confirmed: english_requirement (no language test is published for this scheme)
verification.notes: The Rs. 50,000 monthly allowance, the Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 20,000 contingency grants, the round-trip air fare, visa reimbursement, eligibility, selection procedure and the 31 December 2025 - 31 March 2026 window were confirmed in INSA's official ISRF brochure and announcement PDFs linked from the INSA call page; the 2025-26 window has closed.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a 3-6 month research visit, not a degree or postdoc position: the single most important step is finding and securing a host scientist in India before you apply, because a Letter of Acceptance is part of the package. Money flows per month (Rs. 50,000, with accommodation and medical facilities where the institute offers them) plus two separate contingency grants, and flights and visa fees are outside the cash stipend so do not budget them twice. The scholarship can be taken only once in a five-year period, so pick the host and the timing deliberately.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Researchers aged under 45 from the eight listed countries with 3-5 years of research or teaching experience and a viable host scientist in an Indian institute.
application_readiness_checklist: Re-confirm the eight eligible countries and that you hold no Indian temporary or permanent residency visa
Secure the Indian host supervisor and obtain the Letter of Acceptance on institute letterhead plus the No Objection Certificate from your home institution
Collect the two most recent refereed-journal publications as reprints, not just citations
Check your age against 1 April of the application year (below 45 for this call)
Agree with the host scientist on a realistic 3-6 month research plan that can be reported in writing afterwards
Route the application via your country's implementing agency if one exists, otherwise centrally to INSA
common_rejection_risks: No host scientist secured in advance, or an acceptance letter without No Objection Certificate from the home institution
Applying with only citations instead of reprints of the two recent publications
Proposals without a clear contribution to advanced research, which is the pre-screening criterion
Nationality or residency mismatch, including holding any Indian temporary or permanent visa
Assuming the award is extendable or renewable - it may be availed only once in five years
Late submission to the implementing agency rather than to INSA where no agency exists
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the Rs. 50,000 monthly allowance where the host institute cannot provide accommodation or medical facilities, plus personal living and incidental costs.
document_audit: The endorsement from the Head of the home institution is mandatory on the application itself
The host supervisor's acceptance letter must be on institute letterhead and the home institution must issue a No Objection Certificate
Applications already under consideration elsewhere, such as a Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Fund application, can make you ineligible
Keep the passport valid well beyond the planned visit because the visa is issued on the basis of the award
alerts: The 2025-26 call closed on 31 March 2026, so the next window is expected around 31 December 2026 - prepare documents in advance
The final award intimation rests with DST through INSA, so an implementing-agency approval is not yet a fellowship
Fellowship dates must be jointly finalised with the host scientist after selection, so do not buy non-refundable tickets before the award letter
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Endorse at home institution, secure host acceptance, submit via the partner-country implementing agency or directly to INSA with the scan copy to isrf.dst@insa.nic.in.

official.deadline_note: No fixed calendar deadline: applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies and Indian missions abroad, so timing depends on each mission's local call.
official.status_note: UGC publishes no application window for this scheme on its student corner, which lists only its other fellowship and scholarship schemes; applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies and missions abroad.
benefits: JRF fellowship of Rs. 12,000 per month for the initial two years and Rs. 14,000 per month for the remaining period, subject to the recommendation of a three-member committee and the Commission's approval
RA fellowship of Rs. 16,000 per month (fixed) for four years
Contingency grant of Rs. 12,000 per annum for Science and Rs. 10,000 per annum for Humanities and Social Sciences, rising to Rs. 25,000 and Rs. 20,500 per annum for the remaining period

Departmental assistance of Rs. 3,000 per annum per JRF, escort or handicapped allowance of Rs. 2,000 per annum per JRF, and departmental assistance of 10 percent of the associateship to the host institution for RA

Single-seated hostel accommodation or House Rent Allowance as per the rules of the university or institution; leave of up to 30 days per year plus public holidays, and maternity leave of 135 days at full rates for women awardees
No separate or fixed medical assistance; medical facilities available in the institution or university may be used
eligibility: Students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America
JRF: 35 years for male candidates and 40 years for female candidates as on 1 July of the year of application
JRF academic: at least a high-class master's degree with a second-class bachelor's degree, or a second-class master's degree with a first-class bachelor's degree
RA: 40 years for male applicants and 45 years for female candidates, with a doctorate degree, published research work and evidence of independent research work
The application must be endorsed by the applicant's Indian embassy or mission
Foreign students already studying in India who have completed their master's or doctoral degrees may apply through the university they propose to work with
requirements: Three typed or legibly handwritten copies of the application form
Endorsement by the applicant's Indian embassy or mission for consideration by the Commission
Six-monthly progress reports of the work by the end of June and December, duly signed by the supervisor, head of department and registrar
documents: Three certified copies of the university or college record
Three typed copies of a statement of not more than 500 words describing the research plan
One certified copy of the birth certificate or evidence of date of birth
Three recent passport-size photographs, one stapled to each form
Endorsement by the Indian embassy or mission (or by the proposed host university for applicants already in India)
selection_criteria: Applications are placed before a short-listing or screening committee constituted for the purpose
Short-listed proposals are placed before a selection committee to finalise the proposals for the award

The decision of the Commission is final and binding, and the formal award letter is issued only on receipt of political clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of External Affairs
coverage: JRF fellowship of Rs. 12,000 per month for the initial two years, rising to Rs. 14,000 per month for the remaining period after enhancement
RA fellowship of Rs. 16,000 per month fixed for four years
Annual contingency grants, departmental assistance and escort or handicapped allowance as published
HRA as per the rules of the concerned institution, or single-seated hostel accommodation
application_method: Obtain the application through the Indian embassy or Indian mission in the applicant's country, which screens locally and forwards to the UGC
Foreign students already in India apply through the university they propose to work with, with embassy endorsement
Submit three copies of the form with all enclosures for consideration by the Commission
After award, join under the host institution and submit the Joining Report; later grants are released on the Utilisation Certificate and Statement of Expenditure
official.application_route: Apply through the Indian embassy or mission in the applicant's country, or through the proposed host university for applicants already in India
official.citizenship_residency: Not open to Indian citizens; restricted to students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is exclusively for foreign nationals
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Advanced study and research leading to M.Phil/Ph.D. and postdoctoral research in sciences, humanities and social sciences at Indian universities
official.research_requirement: A statement of not more than 500 words describing the research plan, in three typed copies; RA applicants must have a doctorate with published research work and evidence of independent research work
official.duration: Four years, non-extendable, for both JRF and RA
official.description: The UGC's Junior Research Fellowship and Research Associateship for foreign nationals enables students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America to undertake advanced study and research leading to M.Phil/Ph.D. and postdoctoral research at Indian universities, with a monthly fellowship, annual contingency grant, departmental assistance and HRA per the host institution's rules.
official.program_type: Government research fellowship for foreign nationals

not_confirmed: current (revised) fellowship rates - the published figures come from UGC's XI Plan guidelines document
verification.notes: The JRF and RA rates, contingency grants, departmental assistance, HRA rule, age limits, slot numbers (20 JRF and 7 RA), four-year non-extendable tenure and the embassy-endorsement route were confirmed in UGC's own scheme document 'XIth Plan Guidelines: Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Research Associateship (RA) for Foreign Nationals', linked from the UGC XI Plan Guidelines publications page. The figures are XI-Plan-era rates, so the current stipend and contingency amounts may have been revised upward and could not be re-confirmed against a newer UGC publication.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no portal: the application enters through the Indian embassy or mission in your country, which screens locally before anything reaches the UGC, so build the embassy step into your timeline. The award covers a fellowship plus contingency, departmental assistance and HRA, but it is not a fee waiver, and the formal award letter only comes after political clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of External Affairs. Note the age rule is anchored to 1 July of the application year, with different limits for male and female candidates.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Teachers and advanced students from developing countries in Asia, Africa or Latin America with strong master's or doctoral records who want to pursue M.Phil, PhD or postdoctoral research at an Indian university.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you fall inside the gender-specific age limits calculated on 1 July of the application year (35/40 for JRF, 40/45 for RA)
Contact the Indian embassy or mission in your country early to obtain the current call and application forms
Prepare three complete sets of the form, each with a photograph, the certified record copy, the birth-certificate copy and the 500-word statement in triplicate
If already studying in India, apply through the university you propose to work with, still with embassy endorsement
Keep the research statement within 500 words and make it readable by a screening committee without specialist background
Diarise six-monthly progress-report deadlines for June and December once funded
common_rejection_risks: Missing the embassy endorsement, without which the application is not considered by the Commission
Submitting fewer than three copies of the form or enclosures
Academic combination that does not match the prescribed pattern (high-class master's with second-class bachelor's, or vice versa)
Assuming the provisional intimation is an award - it confers no entitlement until political clearance and the formal award letter
Holding any other paid position during the tenure, which is prohibited
Exceeding the four-year tenure, after which the award automatically ceases and no extension is permissible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and any institutional fees, medical costs beyond what the host university's facilities cover, and personal expenses beyond the HRA or hostel entitlement.
document_audit: The 500-word research statement must be typed and in triplicate, one copy per form set
Birth certificate or evidence of date of birth is a required certified copy because age eligibility is decisive
The embassy or mission endorsement must be on the application itself, so start the consular step early
Grant administration runs through the host university: after the joining report, Utilisation Certificates and Statements of Expenditure gate every later installment
alerts: The published rates come from UGC's XI Plan guidelines, so treat the figures as indicative until UGC reissues them
The Commission may withdraw or cancel an award at any time, and its decision is final and binding
Grant payments are routed through the host institution rather than paid to the fellow directly
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Obtain the form via the Indian embassy or mission, submit three copies with endorsements, then UGC short-listing, selection committee and finally political clearance before the award letter.
